description: Scenario registry for the 23-evals cross-domain acceptance (act_RUNTIME.md rows C1..X1). Each case carries the semantic observable a user would judge and a DETERMINISTIC grader spec. Graders are outcome/constraint-level: none of them accepts or rejects based on an exact tool-call sequence. Mode 'scripted' means exercised through the real app/worker/store with the harness's own deterministic scripted-model fixtures (V2/V4 seam-proof pattern); scripted results are labelled scripted, never live. Live-provider legs run against the local LiteLLM proxy (127.0.0.1:4000/v1 on the host, litellm:4000 on the compose net) through the REAL intake seam (the final_result/TurnInterpretation output tool), inside a DISPOSABLE marked container on the compose infra network — the production credential travels only through the fixture env-file mount, never through a repo file. The ratified evaluation budget (60 requests / 30 minutes / USD 5, first bound wins) bounds every live leg; a live leg that cannot run is reported not_measured with its reason, never as a pass.

budget.stop_policy: first bound reached stops all live legs

cases.interaction: Retry the identical client_request_id after the first turn completed; then reuse the key with different content. The crash-restart leg parks the first turn at the durable reconciling checkpoint on an unknown-status effect, SIGKILLs the worker mid-park, starts a fresh worker, resumes the run deliberately through the product's sanctioned EngineClient.resume_run surface (never blind launch recovery) and resolves the uncertain step through the real reconciliation producer RecoveryService.aresolve_step (FINAL_SUCCEEDED).
cases.observable: One message, one run row, one intake result across the crash: the uncertain effect is never re-dispatched (journal begin/effect markers exactly once) and the restart adds no extra planner model call; the reconciliation resolution moves the step out of outcome_unknown to a terminal state and the run reaches terminal; the retry deduplicates onto the same message and run identities and the conflicting key reuse is a structured 409, never a duplicate effect.

checks: identical retry returns deduplicated with the same message/run identities
changed payload on the same key is a structured 409
exactly one conversation_messages row and one job_runs row for the key
zero effects duplicated

cases.interaction: Steer during a two-call batch (first call parked in-flight), then send Pause; release the in-flight call.
cases.observable: Pause is deterministic (no planner call needed); the new command starts only after the applicable steering/scope check and is never dispatched after the pause; the in-flight effect completes honestly at most once; natural-language steering stays pending, not silently dropped. The run ends terminal (succeeded) with agent.completed stopped_by=pause, no additional planner model call.

checks: exactly one fixture.priv effect begins and completes once
the second call never begins after the pause
run ends terminal (succeeded) with agent.completed stopped_by=pause, no additional planner model call
steering row persisted with no applied timestamp (pending vs applied honest)
